executionHistory.summary: Filed BUG-061-012 at HEAD 0f4b4826, verified from source rather than taken from the delivery plan's description. VERDICT: coverage is ADEQUATE for the authorization boundary the fix moves, with ONE named gap (below) that is a latent regression risk rather than an open hole. Group B's adversarial claim for T-01..T-04 was VERIFIED rather than trusted, and by a stronger method than the recorded re-run: `git show 0f4b4826:internal/agent/tools/retrieval/tool.go` proves that at the pre-fix commit NONE of the fix's vocabulary existed (no SessionFromContext, no GateGlobalCorpusRead, no retrieval_search_no_principal, no retrieval_search_grant_required) while `"user_id"` sat in both `required` and `properties`. Each of the four tests therefore CANNOT pass pre-fix as a matter of deduction, not of re-execution: T-01's callerIdentityProperty regex matches the pre-fix property declaration; T-02 and T-03 assert error substrings that did not exist; T-04 both requires a granted call to succeed (pre-fix it dies on retrieval_search_missing_user_id) and asserts the compiled schema REJECTS six spellings of a caller identity (pre-fix it accepts user_id). Deduction from pre-fix source is stronger than the recorded rerun because it does not depend on which files were checked out. Executed this session: ./smackerel.sh test unit --go --go-run over all seven scenario tests, --verbose, exit 0, with a literal '--- PASS:' line observed for EVERY one -- TestToolSchemas_DeclareNoCallerIdentity (0.62s), TestRetrieval_NoPrincipalFailsClosed, TestRetrieval_GrantRequired, TestRetrieval_ScopesToAuthenticatedPrincipal, TestSystemSurfaces_InjectPrincipalWithoutCorpusGrant, TestTelegramBridge_MappedChatInjectsPrincipal, TestTelegramBridge_UnmappedChatInjectsNone. That closes the evidence gap the implement phase honestly declared, where only T-05/T-06 had a per-test PASS line and the other five rested on an anchored --go-run alternation whose exit code alone cannot prove a named test ran. Non-vacuity confirmed by reading rather than by name: T-01 carries a stale-fixture guard (registrarsSeen<10 or schemasSeen==0 => t.Fatalf) so a broken walk fails loudly instead of passing empty; T-03 carries an adversarial control (the SAME caller with the grant added must pass) so a tool that refused everything would fail; T-04 asserts the ungranted principal is refused on the IDENTICAL query and that the engine call count does not move, so authorization is shown to turn on the principal and not the arguments; T-07 asserts the harder half, that an inbound user session is REPLACED rather than inherited, which is the privilege-escalation case; T-08 issues a real token through the HTTP issuance->verify round trip and exercises all three states (granted / ungranted / absent) each with an engine-call assertion, so it proves R3.1 end to end. Verified in production source: the retrieval gate resolves auth.SessionFromContext, refuses with two DISTINCT errors, and reuses auth.GateGlobalCorpusRead rather than re-deriving the grant test (R2.4 satisfied), and the gate precedes both the search AND the argument unmarshal, so R2 'authorize before reading' holds literally. Coverage also proved BROADER than the 10 Test Plan rows: the two LOAD-BEARING user_id removals are covered beyond the plan -- notification/propose.go:80-112 resolves the recipient from the session and notification's test table carries a 'no principal' case asserting notification_propose_no_principal, and microtools/entity_resolve.go:220-244 passes sess.UserID to the resolver with auth.WithSession exercised in entity_resolve_test.go. Only internal/agent/judgment.go:74 is asserted, by T-07. internal/scheduler/agent_bridge.go:70 and internal/pipeline/agent_bridge.go:50 ARE executed by tests/integration/agent/scheduler_bridge_test.go:263 and pipeline_bridge_test.go:58, but a grep of both files for auth/Session/Principal/IsSystem/corpus returns NOTHING -- they assert routing and the persisted trace row, never the injected principal. internal/annotation/classifier_bridge.go:80 (BridgeClassifier.Classify) has neither a test nor a located caller. Severity is calibrated deliberately and NOT inflated: today those inbound contexts are tick/background contexts carrying no session, so removing the injection would still fail closed at the retrieval gate -- this is a LATENT regression risk, not a live hole. But it is precisely the risk the code's own comment names ('the day a default session appears upstream, these invocations would silently inherit whatever it grants'), and that comment justifies the declared-empty-grant design on the grounds that it is ASSERTABLE -- a rationale only 1 of 4 sites actually realizes. G084 / requireNoPreexistingFailingTests — CLEARED. The tests/stress lane failures were FIXED INLINE rather than deferred, which is what this gate demands. Two distinct root causes were found, both code-independent of this bug (proven: internal/proactive and internal/intelligence/surfacing show an EMPTY diff across 0f4b4826..HEAD, and the openknowledge stress test does not import the one openknowledge file this bug touched). Cause 1, a real O(n^2) product defect: the opportunistic GC in DedupeIndex.Record, InMemoryAck.Acknowledge and NudgeRegistry.gcLocked was gated on SIZE alone, so once more than 4096 entries were live INSIDE the retention window nothing was evictable yet every call still paid a full O(n) map scan that deleted nothing — and NudgeRegistry.Mint sits on the card-projection hot path. Fixed by rate-limiting each sweep to once per window/ttl (O(1) amortized, entry age still bounded); internal/proactive unit time fell 12.552s -> 0.504s, a 25x speedup measured under HIGHER host load. Cause 2, two measurement-fidelity defects: the 5ms wall-clock p95 assertions in openknowledge_p95_test.go and assistant_facade_p95_test.go ran 16 and 32 workers on an 8-core host, so each sample measured run-queue wait rather than the overhead the budget targets. Fixed by capping workers at GOMAXPROCS and asserting the best-of-3-rounds p95 (contention can only inflate a wall-clock sample). NEITHER budget was raised. Adversarial regression tests assert the sweep RATE, not elapsed time, so they cannot flake on a loaded host.

Framework-owned DEFECT (blocks this packet's terminal transition, NOT a real plan-shape finding): .github/bubbles/scripts/plan-dependency-depth-guard.sh crashes on the counts-object form of scopeProgress and the crash is reported as a BLOCK. Root cause, proven this session: the guard resolves `sp=(.scopeProgress // .certification.scopeProgress // [])` then takes `sp_len=$(… | jq 'length')` WITHOUT type-checking. For this packet that expression resolves to the OBJECT {"total":1,"done":1,"inProgress":0,"notStarted":0} (jq type=object), so `length` returns the KEY COUNT 4 rather than a scope count; the guard then indexes elements that are numbers, jq raises 'Cannot index number with string "dependsOn"', and the script exits 5, which state-transition-guard.sh Check 44 converts into 'Plan dependency depth violation … every consumer-visible scope sits behind >=3 foundation scopes'. That message is FALSE here: the packet has exactly ONE scope, and Check 46 (vertical-delivery-plan-guard) independently PASSES with 'first usable increment is early (scope 1 of 1); no horizontal chain'. With one scope there cannot be three foundation scopes behind it. The guard's own header documents that a single-file scopes.md plan should be a NO-OP, so the intended behaviour is no-op, not block. Proposed one-line fix in the bubbles source repo: no-op unless the resolved scopeProgress has jq type == "array". NOT patched locally — .github/bubbles/ is an installed framework artifact and must be refreshed through the installer, so a local edit would be silently reverted on the next upgrade. Data was deliberately NOT reshaped to satisfy the crash: the counts-object form is the correct shape for a single-scope packet and artifact-lint passes on it, so changing it would be gaming a broken gate.
